title: Indian Engineer, Two Firms Indicted in Baltimore Bridge Collapse
excerpt: DOJ charges Synergy Marine and technical superintendent Radhakrishnan Karthik Nair for safety cover-ups in Dali ship disaster
body:
**Criminal Charges After Two Years**

Federal prosecutors unsealed criminal indictments on Monday against Singapore-based Synergy Marine, its sister company Synergy Maritime, and Indian national Radhakrishnan Karthik Nair — the technical superintendent responsible for the M/V Dali container ship that slammed into Baltimore's Francis Scott Key Bridge on March 26, 2024, killing six construction workers.

The U.S. Department of Justice alleges the defendants conspired to defraud the United States by concealing dangerous safety conditions aboard the Dali. Prosecutors say Nair and the companies knew the ship relied on a non-redundant flushing pump that caused catastrophic electrical blackouts. A loose wire in the ship's electrical system triggered two power failures, cutting propulsion and steering as the vessel approached the bridge.

**Cover-Up Alleged**

Investigators say the defendants falsified safety records and obstructed the probe into the disaster, which caused an estimated $4.3–5.2 billion in damage and shut down the Port of Baltimore for weeks. Maryland reached a $2.25 billion civil settlement with the vessel's operator, but the criminal case now raises the stakes dramatically.

Nair, who oversaw the Dali's technical operations from India, faces charges of conspiracy and making false statements to federal investigators. The companies face similar conspiracy charges.
nri_angle: The indictment of an Indian national in one of America's worst infrastructure disasters raises questions about liability for Indian professionals managing global maritime operations.
author: Diaspora Desk
